provenance: Demonstration rules written by Team ANGARIS for the ASTRA Health prototype. They are not clinical criteria, not a NASA protocol and not validated. They only decide which predefined next steps are proposed and when contact with medical support is suggested. They never name a condition, a medication or a treatment.

levels.label: Monitor
levels.text: Log the symptom and keep monitoring.

levels.label: Inform crew medical officer
levels.text: The crew medical officer should review this.

levels.label: Medical support recommended
levels.text: Contact with the ground medical team is recommended.

levels.label: Medical support now
levels.text: Contact the ground medical team now.

warningSigns.label: Confusion, trouble speaking or unusual drowsiness
Sudden weakness or numbness on one side of the body

steps.text: Record the symptom in today's journal check-in (FUTURE 01).
Repeat this assessment within 12 hours (demonstration interval), or sooner if anything changes.
Repeat this assessment within 2 hours (demonstration interval).
Take a vital-sign check (heart rate, SpO₂, temperature) and review it on the Monitoring screen.
Keep the crew member accompanied until the crew medical officer has reviewed the situation.
Queue a PRIORITY report to the ground medical team (Earth Link).
Queue an URGENT report to the ground medical team now. The crew medical officer reviews without waiting for the reply.
Hold EVA participation for this crew member until reviewed (checked by FUTURE 04).
Do the visual acuity self-check and record the result (FUTURE 03).
Review the journal trend for this symptom with the crew medical officer.

rules.description: Every reported symptom is logged and reassessed.
At least one warning sign is present.
The crew member rates the symptom as severe.
The crew member cannot perform their duties.
Any change in vision is reported.
The symptom has lasted 48 hours or more (demonstration threshold).
The same symptom appears in the journal on 3 or more of the last 7 days (demonstration threshold).

evidenceMap.note: Which official HRP risks are shown as scientific context for each symptom. The association was chosen by Team ANGARIS; it is not a NASA statement and not a diagnosis.
